title: Detection of an Intermediate in the Unfolding Process of the N-Terminal Domain of TDP-43.
authors: Marzi, Isabella; Pieraccini, Giuseppe; Bemporad, Francesco; Chiti, Fabrizio
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物物理实验研究TDP-43 N端结构域去折叠中间态，虽涉及蛋白-DNA结合蛋白但未聚焦TF-DNA互作，且方法以实验为主、仅引用MD模拟，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模创新。
abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is a nuclear protein accumulating in intraneuronal cytoplasmic inclusions associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, frontotemporal lobar degeneration with tau-negative/ubiquitin-positive inclusions, and limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy. Oligomerization of full-length TDP-43, driven by its N-terminal domain (NTD), is essential for its function, but aberrant self-assembly also promotes liquid-liquid phase separation and formation of solid inclusions. Building on recent all-atom molecular dynamics simulations and using various biophysical approaches, we identified a partially unfolded state accumulating during unfolding of TDP-43 NTD, before the major energy barrier of unfolding is crossed. Intrinsic fluorescence spectroscopy coupled to a stopped-flow device at high urea concentration reveals that the intermediate state has a fluorescence emission distinct from those of the native and unfolded states and forms within the 14 ms dead time. Conventional fluorescence spectroscopy shows it still accumulates at moderate urea concentration. Circular dichroism and H/D exchange results show a species with an intermediate content of secondary structure and a distorted beta-sheet, whereas SYPRO orange fluorescence indicates an open conformation with more exposed hydrophobic regions compared to the native state. Importantly, this intermediate is observed even at low protein concentration, when TDP-43 NTD is largely monomeric, indicating that its formation is independent of the initial TDP-43 NTD oligomeric state. Dynamic light scattering at high protein concentration shows that the intermediate is a partially folded dimer. The intermediate forms upon chemical denaturation and does not occur under thermal unfolding. Overall, the findings highlight the presence of one more partially folded state for TDP-43 NTD, underlining its high structural plasticity and suggesting that its distinct unfolding pathway may play a critical role in both its functional and pathological behaviors.
abstract_zh: TAR DNA结合蛋白43（TDP-43）是一种核蛋白，在肌萎缩侧索硬化、伴有tau阴性/泛素阳性包涵体的额颞叶变性以及边缘系统为主的年龄相关TDP-43脑病中，积累于神经元内胞浆包涵体中。全长TDP-43的寡聚化由其N端结构域（NTD）驱动，对其功能至关重要，但异常自组装也促进液-液相分离（liquid-liquid phase separation）和固体包涵体的形成。基于近期全原子分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟，并利用多种生物物理方法，我们鉴定出在TDP-43 NTD去折叠过程中、跨越主要能量屏障之前积累的部分去折叠状态。在高尿素浓度下，与停流装置联用的内源荧光光谱显示，该中间态具有不同于天然态和去折叠态的荧光发射，并在14毫秒死时间内形成。常规荧光光谱显示，在中等尿素浓度下它仍会积累。圆二色光谱和氢/氘交换结果表明，存在一种具有中间二级结构含量和扭曲β-折叠的物种，而SYPRO橙荧光则表明，与天然态相比，其构象开放，疏水区域暴露更多。重要的是，即使在低蛋白浓度下（此时TDP-43 NTD主要以单体形式存在），该中间态也能被观察到，表明其形成不依赖于初始TDP-43 NTD的寡聚状态。在高蛋白浓度下的动态光散射显示，该中间态为部分折叠的二聚体。该中间态在化学变性时形成，而在热去折叠过程中不出现。总体而言，这些发现突显了TDP-43 NTD存在另一种部分折叠状态，强调其高结构可塑性，并提示其独特的去折叠途径可能在其功能性和病理性行为中发挥关键作用。
